Ashraf Hamed Al Mamari (Group CEO) | industry = [[oil and gas industry|Oil and gas]] | products = {{hlist|Polypropylene|polyethylene|intermediates|derivatives|refined products}} | services = | revenue = | operating_income = | net_income = | assets = | equity = | owner = [[Government of Oman]] | num_employees = | parent = | divisions = | subsidiaries = | website = {{url|oq.com}} | footnotes = }} '''OQ''', formerly known as '''Oman Oil Company''', is an energy [[investment company]] headquartered in [[Muscat]], [[Oman]]. It is a wholly owned subsidiary of the [[Government of Oman]] through the [[Oman Investment Authority]] [[state-owned enterprise]]. OQ is involved in sectors such as infrastructure and transportation for energy, oil refining, petrochemical production, oil marketing, and power generating. It operates in 17 countries.{{Cite web |date=2021-11-20 |title=OQ posts $777mn profit for H1, revenues surge to $10bn |url=https://www.muscatdaily.com/2021/11/20/oq-posts-777mn-profit-for-h1-revenues-surge-to-10bn/ |access-date=2023-03-29 |website=Muscat Daily |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Rahman |first=Fareed |date=2021-12-07 |title=Saudi Aramco's trading arm signs agreement with Oman's OQ on new opportunities |url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/business/energy/2021/12/07/saudi-aramcos-trading-arm-signs-agreement-with-omans-oq-on-new-opportunities/ |access-date=2023-03-29 |website=The National |language=en}} As of June 2023, OQ produces more than 246,000 barrels of oil per day.{{Cite web|url=https://timesofoman.com/article/118164-oq-group-produces-218000-barrels-per-day-of-oil|title=OQ Group produces 218,000 barrels per day of oil|website=Times of Oman}} ==History== ===1982 to 2000=== OQ was founded as the Oman Refinery Company in 1982.{{Cite web|url=https://oq.com/en/about-oq/company/our-journey|title=Our Journey & History | OQ|website=oq.com}} In 1996, Oman Oil Company was established by the Government of Oman.{{Cite news | title = Oman Oil Company Appoints CEO | agency = Zawya | url = http://www.zawya.com/story.cfm/sidZAWYA20060620080151 | date = 2004-08-30 | accessdate = 2011-01-06 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110617080713/http://www.zawya.com/story.cfm/sidZAWYA20060620080151 | archive-date = 2011-06-17 | url-status = dead }} A separate company for gas, named Oman Gas Company, was established in 2000. ===2002 to 2010=== In 2003, Oman Oil Marketing Company (Oman Oil) was founded. Oman Trading International, a trading division, was established in 2006. Oman Refineries and Petrochemicals Co. was created in 2007 with the merger of Oman Refinery Company and Sohar Refinery Company. In 2009, Oman Oil Company Exploration & Production was founded. In 2010, the Programme Apple was initiated which aimed to integrate Oman Refineries and Petrochemicals Company, Oman [[Polypropylene]] Co., and Aromatics Oman Ltd. In the same year, Oman Oil Company signed a joint-venture with JBF Industries to erect a [[Terephthalic acid]]-PTA plant.{{cite web|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424052748704107204575038494052484432|title=Oman Oil Sign Joint Venture Pact|date=February 1, 2010|work=JBF Industries|accessdate=January 24, 2019}} ===2011 to 2020=== Following the initial phase of integration, Orpic was founded in 2011. In 2013, OQ acquired a German-based company, Oxea.{{cite news | url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-09-22/oman-said-to-consider-sale-of-3-billion-german-chemicals-unit | title=Oman Considers Sale of $3 Billion German Chemicals Unit | newspaper=Bloomberg.com | date=22 September 2021 }} OOC signed an exploration and production agreement with [[BP]] in 2013, to further develop the [[Khazzan-Makarem gas field]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2013/12/17/business/international/bp-and-oman-agree-to-develop-gas-field.html|title=BP and Oman Agree to Jointly Develop a Gas Field, With Bigger Goals in Mind|date=December 16, 2013|work=New York Times|accessdate=January 24, 2019}} In 2014, construction of the Sohar Refinery Improvement Project started.{{Cite web|url=https://www.hydrocarbons-technology.com/projects/sohar-refinery-improvement-project/|title=Sohar Refinery Improvement Project - Hydrocarbons Technology|website=www.hydrocarbons-technology.com}} In 2016, OOC secured a $4 billion [[loan]] to invest into various projects over the coming years.{{cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/oman-petroleum-idUSL8N19L1SY|title=UPDATE 1-Oman oil company PDO raises $4 bln of project financing|date=June 29, 2016|work=Reuters|accessdate=January 24, 2019}} In the following year OOC signed a [[memorandum]] of understanding with [[Spain]]'s [[Eni]].{{cite web|url=http://markets.on.nytimes.com/research/stocks/fundamentals/drawFiling.asp?docKey=137-000117494718000586-1VD24C75ERIO3Q0KSIA42QKG3C&docFormat=HTM&formType=20-F|title=Form 20-F|date=|work=The New York Times|accessdate=January 24, 2019|archive-date=January 25, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190125130838/http://markets.on.nytimes.com/research/stocks/fundamentals/drawFiling.asp?docKey=137-000117494718000586-1VD24C75ERIO3Q0KSIA42QKG3C&docFormat=HTM&formType=20-F|url-status=dead}} In 2017, a [[joint venture]] between [[Kuwait Petroleum International]] and OQ was announced for the development of Duqm Refinery & Petrochemical Complex.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nsenergybusiness.com/projects/duqm-refinery-and-petrochemicals-project/|title=Duqm Refinery and Petrochemicals Project - NS Energy}} In the same year, OQ's subsidiary, Oman Tank Terminal Company (OTTCO), began construction of a crude oil storage terminal near Raz Markaz.{{Cite web|url=https://www.hydrocarbons-technology.com/projects/ras-markaz-crude-oil-storage-terminal/|title=Ras Markaz Crude Oil Storage Terminal - Hydrocarbons Technology|website=www.hydrocarbons-technology.com}} In 2018, Oman Oil Company sold 10% of its 40% stake in the Khazzan gas field to [[Malaysia]]'s [[Petronas]] and signed two concessions/agreements with [[Occidental Petroleum]] (Oxy).{{cite web|url=https://blogs.wsj.com/moneybeat/2018/10/19/energy-journal-crude-prices-lose-steam-on-rising-stocks/|title=Crude Prices Lose Steam on Rising Stocks—Energy Journal|date=October 19, 2018|work=The Wall Street Journal|accessdate=January 24, 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/malaysias-petronas-set-to-buy-10-stake-in-giant-oman-gas-field-1539888611|title=Malaysia's Petronas Set to Buy 10% Stake in Giant Oman Gas Field|date=October 28, 2018|work=The Wall Street Journal|accessdate=January 24, 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-global-oil/oil-falls-u-s-crude-dips-below-50-on-oversupply-fears-idUSKBN1OG01L|title=Oman signs exploration agreements with Occidental Petroleum|date=December 16, 2018|work=Reuters|accessdate=January 24, 2019}} In November 2018, OOC announced that the company will be merged with refining company [[Oman Refinery Company|Orpic]], which had been created in 2011 to operate Oman's downstream assets.{{cite web|url=https://www.theoilandgasyear.com/news/oman-oil-company-orpic-to-merge/|title=Oman Oil Company, Orpic to merge|date=November 19, 2018|work=The Oil and Gas Year|accessdate=January 29, 2019}} The NAKHLA programme was initiated in 2018.{{Cite web|url=https://www.argusmedia.com/en/news/2036632-oman-to-merge-oil-petrochemical-firms-under-oq-brand|title=Oman to merge oil, petrochemical firms under OQ brand | Argus Media|date=December 18, 2019|website=www.argusmedia.com}} The construction of the [[Duqm Refinery]] began the same year, as did the groundwork for the Salalah LPG and Salalah Ammonia Projects.{{Cite web|url=https://www.hydrocarbons-technology.com/projects/salalah-liquefied-petroleum-gas-project-dhofar/|title=Salalah Liquefied Petroleum Gas Project, Dhofar, Oman|website=www.hydrocarbons-technology.com}} Orpic Group merged with Oman Oil Company in 2019, and the combined business was given the moniker OQ.{{cite web|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/hopes-dashed-for-a-middle-east-markets-bonanza-11544965200|title=Hopes Dashed For a Middle East Markets Bonanza|date=December 16, 2018|work=The Wall Street Journal|accessdate=January 29, 2019}} OQ is an acronym for "Opportunity and Quality." In 2019, Oman Gas Company was incorporated into the OQ brand and was renamed OQ Gas Networks (OQGN).{{Cite web |title=OQGN |url=https://oqgn.com/journey.html |access-date=2023-06-28 |website=oqgn.com}}{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=OQGN launches its new corporate identity |url=https://timesofoman.com/article/125073-oqgn-launches-its-new-corporate-identity |access-date=2023-06-28 |website=Times of Oman |language=en}} In January 2020, the State Budget allocated funds to assist OQ Subsidiary, Oman Tank Terminal Company (OTTCO), with the Ras Markaz crude oil storage terminal that would become an international storage hub and strategically locate Oman in the [[Indian Ocean]].{{Cite web |last=Prabhu |first=Conrad |title=$25bln worth strategic projects to fuel Omans economic growth |url=https://www.zawya.com/en/business/25bln-worth-strategic-projects-to-fuel-omans-economic-growth-co2b8jv1 |access-date=2023-06-29 |website=www.zawya.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2020-06-18 |title=Oman steps up plan for Middle East's biggest oil-tank farm |url=https://www.gulf-times.com/story/665994/oman-steps-up-plan-for-middle-easts-biggest-oil-tank-farm |access-date=2023-06-29 |website=Gulf Times |language=en}} Funds were also placed from the budget into the Liwa Plastic Industries Complex, a OQ investment. In May 2020, the commissioning phase commenced.{{Cite web |title=Oman's $6.7bn petchem project enters commissioning phase |url=http://www.tradearabia.com/news/OGN_367868.html |access-date=2023-06-29 |website=www.tradearabia.com}} Production increases were planned for OQC in Germany for 2021. The OQ announced in May 2020 the intention to add 30% total production for the coming year.{{Cite web |last=Prabhu |first=Conrad |title=Oman-owned chemicals giant eyes new capacity growth in 2021 |url=https://www.zawya.com/en/business/oman-owned-chemicals-giant-eyes-new-capacity-growth-in-2021-syl3rafj |access-date=2023-07-12 |website=www.zawya.com |language=en}} In June 2020, Oxea was fully integrated into a group of eight other companies to create OQ, after the full process had begun in 2018.{{Cite web |title=OQ completes integration of international assets |url=https://www.tradearabia.com/news/OGN_368791.html |access-date=2023-07-12 |website=www.tradearabia.com}}{{Cite web |date=2020-02-14 |title=Oman's oil and gas sector after Sultan Qaboos |url=https://www.oilandgasmiddleeast.com/exploration-production/drilling-production/36154-omans-oil-and-gas-sector-after-sultan-qaboos |access-date=2023-07-12 |website=Oil & Gas Middle East}}{{Cite web |date=2020-06-12 |title=Middle East petrochemical consolidations pick up pace {{!}} Argus Media |url=https://www.argusmedia.com/en//news/2113851-middle-east-petrochemical-consolidations-pick-up-pace |access-date=2023-07-12 |website=www.argusmedia.com |language=en}} In August 2020, OQ and the Ministry of Heritage and Tourism collaborated to announce the opening of a tourist centre at the archaeological site in the Wilayat of Al Dibba.{{Cite web|url=https://www.refiningandpetrochemicalsme.com/people/28950-oq-office-of-minister-of-state-and-governor-of-musandam-ink-moc-to-finance-social-investment-projects|title=OQ, office of minister of state and governor of Musandam ink MoC to finance social investment projects|work=Refining & Petrochemicals Middle East |date=24 August 2020 }} The OQ also signed a Memorandum of Cooperation (MoC) with the Minister of Education and Jusoor Foundation to manage and run the Liwa Science and Innovation Center.{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=OQ, ministry sign pact to manage, operate Liwa Science & Innovation Centre |url=https://timesofoman.com/article/93151-oq-ministry-sign-pact-to-manage-operate-liwa-science-innovation-centre |access-date=2023-09-08 |website=Times of Oman |language=en}} ===2021 to present=== In January 2021, Group CEO of OQ, Musub al Mahrouqi submitted his resignation which would be effective as of March that year. In response, the Board of Directors appointed the position of GCEO to Talal bin Hamid al Awfi to take over the responsibilities starting immediately.{{Cite web |title=Oman State Oil Firm OQ Names Talal Al Awfi as Acting CEO |url=https://news.bloomberglaw.com/esg/oman-state-oil-firm-oq-names-talal-al-awfi-as-acting-ceo |access-date=2023-08-15 |website=news.bloomberglaw.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2021-01-27 |title=OQ names new Acting Group CEO |url=https://www.omanobserver.om/article/4415/Business/oq-names-new-acting-group-ceo |access-date=2023-08-15 |website=Oman Observer |language=en}} Head of Procurement at OQ is Ahmed Al Azkawi.{{Cite web |title=Major oil, gas companies join efforts to boost level of Omanisation |url=https://businessgateways.com/news/2021/03/22/Major-oil-gas-companies-join-boost-Omanisation |access-date=2023-08-15 |website=businessgateways.com |language=en-gb |archive-date=2023-08-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230815130227/https://businessgateways.com/news/2021/03/22/Major-oil-gas-companies-join-boost-Omanisation |url-status=dead }} OQ sold its stake in [[Bina Refinery|Bina refinery]] in March 2021, eventually giving its partner [[Bharat Petroleum|Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd.]] (BPCL) full control of [[Bharat Oman Refinery Limited|BORL]].{{Cite web |date=2021-03-21 |title=Privatisation-bound BPCL acquires OQ's stake in Bina refinery |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/privatisation-bound-bpcl-acquires-oq-s-stake-in-bina-refinery-121033101018_1.html |access-date=2023-11-07 |website=Business Standard}}{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2021-02-11 |title=BPCL takes control of Bina Refinery; buys out Omani company's stake at ₹27 a share |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/bpcl-takes-control-of-bina-refinery-buys-out-omani-companys-stake-at-27-a-share/article33807902.ece |access-date=2023-11-07 |website=BusinessLine |language=en}} In September 2021, an announcement was made that OQ was considering sale of its German subsidiary, Oxea, a chemicals business, for about $3 billion. OQ Chemicals has two manufacturing sites in Germany that make a range of oxo intermediates and derivatives. In October 2021, OQ, [[Marubeni]] Corporation, Linde, and Dutco decided to explore the possibility of producing green ammonia and [[green hydrogen]] in Salalah.{{Cite web|url=https://www.marubeni.com/en/news/|title=Marubeni Signs Joint Development Agreement for Green Hydrogen & Green Ammonia Production Infrastructure in Oman|website=www.marubeni.com}} In December 2021, Liwa Plastics Industries Complex (LPIC) project in Sohar was inaugurated.{{Cite web|url=https://www.polymerupdate.com/news/Plant/14Dec2021/1144617/oman’s-oq-to-unveil-the-$7bn-lpic-project-on-december-20|title=Oman's OQ to unveil the $7bn LPIC project on December 20|website=Polymerupdate.com}} The work on the project started in May 2020.{{Cite web|url=https://www.argusmedia.com/en/news/2282507-oman-to-inaugurate-7bn-liwa-plastics-project-next-week|title=Oman to inaugurate $7bn Liwa Plastics project next week | Argus Media|date=December 12, 2021|website=www.argusmedia.com}} With two polyethylene facilities, it has the capacity to produce 880,000 tonnes of [[linear low-density polyethylene]] (LLDPE) and [[high-density polyethylene]] (HDPE) annually. [[SABIC|Saudi Basic Industries Corp]] (SABIC) and OQ signed a [[Memorandum of Understanding]] (MoU) to study the possibility of building a petrochemical project in the Duqm Free Zone.{{Cite web|url=https://www.spglobal.com/commodityinsights/en/market-insights/latest-news/petrochemicals/120821-saudi-arabias-sabic-omans-oq-to-explore-petrochemical-project-in-duqm|title=Saudi Arabia's SABIC, Oman's OQ to explore petrochemical project in Duqm|first=Dania|last=Saadi|date=December 8, 2021|website=www.spglobal.com}} OQ and TotalEnergies formed Marsa LNG, an integrated energy company, in December 2021, which began producing LNG from Block 10 in January 2023 with a 33.19% interest.{{Cite web |last=Ugal |first=Nishant |date=2023-01-20 |title=Shell starts gas production from prolific Middle East onshore asset |url=https://www.upstreamonline.com/production/shell-starts-gas-production-from-prolific-middle-east-onshore-asset/2-1-1391025 |access-date=2023-11-17 |website=Upstream Online {{!}} Latest oil and gas news |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=TotalEnergies, Oman's OQ set up LNG company |url=https://www.naturalgasworld.com/totalenergies-omans-oq-set-up-lng-company-95047 |access-date=2023-11-17 |website=www.naturalgasworld.com}}{{Cite web |last=Rani |first=Archana |date=2022-03-01 |title=Oman plans to award oil and gas blocks to boost production |url=https://www.offshore-technology.com/news/oman-award-blocks-production/ |access-date=2023-11-17 |website=Offshore Technology |language=en-US}} Shell also signed a concession agreement to operate 53.45% of Block 10.{{Cite web |last=Saadi |first=Dania |date=2021-12-21 |title=Shell, other partners to develop gas from Oman's Saih Rawl field with startup in 2 years |url=https://www.spglobal.com/commodityinsights/en/market-insights/latest-news/natural-gas/122121-shell-other-partners-to-develop-gas-from-omans-saih-rawl-field-with-startup-in-2-years |access-date=2023-11-17 |website=www.spglobal.com |language=en}} In May 2022, [[Trend Micro]] and OQ inked a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU), under which Trend Micro would secure OQ's digital infrastructure from cyber threats.{{cite news |id={{ProQuest|2671679320}} |date=31 May 2022 |title=Trend Micro reinforces strategic partnership with OQ |url=https://timesofoman.com/article/117397-trend-micro-reinforces-strategic-partnership-with-oq |work=Times of Oman }} In July 2022, OQ signed an agreement with the Ministry of Higher Education, Research, and Innovation to fund the construction of vocational colleges with an allocation of OMR 200,000.{{Cite web|url=https://www.zawya.com/en/press-release/companies-news/oq-and-ministry-of-education-sign-two-agreements-rjoah807|title=OQ and Ministry of Education sign two agreements|first=Press|last=Release|website=www.zawya.com}} A contract for the exploration and development of natural gas resources in Block 11 was signed by OQ, Shell and [[TotalEnergies]] in September 2022. Shell has a 67.5% stake, OQ 10% and TotalEnergies 22.5%.{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2022-09-15 |title=Oman Inks Deal With Shell, OQ, And TotalEnergies For Gas Exploration In Block 11 |url=https://www.forbesmiddleeast.com/industry/energy/oman-signs-deal-with-shell-oman-oq-totalenergies-for-gas-exploration |access-date=2023-11-17 |website=Forbes ME |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last=Devarasetti |first=Hasini |date=2022-09-16 |title=Oman signs exploration deal with Shell for Block 11 |url=https://www.offshore-technology.com/news/oman-exploration-shell-block-11/ |access-date=2023-11-17 |website=Offshore Technology |language=en-US}} The companies have previously signed a similar agreement for neighbouring Block 10. In June 2023, OQ signed an agreement with [[DEME]] and Hydrom for the project development of [[Hyport Duqm]] for the engineering of 150 square metres and the construction of the [[renewable energy]] and downstream sites required for green [[hydrogen production]] and green ammonia plants.{{Cite web |title=Hydrom awards $10bn contracts to develop new hydrogen projects |date=22 June 2023 |url=https://www.nsenergybusiness.com/news/hydrom-new-hydrogen-projects-in-oman/ |access-date=2023-10-05 |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last= |first= |last2= |first2= |date=2023-06-21 |title=Oman's Hydrom inks two agreements for green hydrogen production |url=https://www.zawya.com/en/projects/industry/omans-hydrom-inks-two-agreements-for-green-hydrogen-production-hlyoyq03 |access-date=2023-10-05 |website=www.zawya.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Benny |first=John |date=2023-06-22 |title=Oman's Hydrom signs agreements worth $10bn to develop green hydrogen plants |url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/business/energy/2023/06/22/omans-hydrom-signs-agreements-worth-10bn-to-develop-green-hydrogen-plants/ |access-date=2023-10-05 |website=The National |language=en}} In August 2023, OQ signed LNG supply agreements with [[Shell plc|Shell]]. OQ is expected to supply 0.8 million tonnes per year of LNG to Shell for 10 years from 2025 and 0.75 million tonnes per year for 4 years from 2026.{{Cite web |title=Oman LNG pens LNG supply deals with Shell, OQ |url=https://www.naturalgasworld.com/oman-lng-pens-lng-supply-deals-with-shell-oq-106951 |access-date=2023-10-05 |website=www.naturalgasworld.com}}{{Cite web |last=Kindi |first=Hibba al |date=2023-08-31 |title=Oman LNG signs pacts to supply LNG to Shell and OQ Trading |url=https://www.zawya.com/en/projects/oil-and-gas/oman-lng-signs-pacts-to-supply-lng-to-shell-and-oq-trading-djkled3l |access-date=2023-10-05 |website=www.zawya.com |language=en}} In October 2023, OQ Gas Networks IPO listing hit a record high and was the third largest listed company on the MSX.{{Cite web |last=Ajmi |first=Nasrulah Al |date=2023-10-24 |title=OQGN’s record-breaking IPO lists on Muscat Stock Exchange |url=https://www.omanobserver.om/article/1144694/business/energy/oqgns-record-breaking-ipo-lists-on-muscat-stock-exchange |access-date=2026-06-12 |website=Oman Observer |language=en}} The IPO was oversubscribed about 14 times and investors bought 2.1 billion shares, a 49% stake, raising OMR 288 million.{{Cite web |last= |date=2023-10-12 |title=Oman’s OQ Gas Networks draws $10 billion in orders for IPO |url=https://gulfnews.com/business/markets/omans-oq-gas-networks-draws-10-billion-in-orders-for-ipo-1.98704698 |access-date=2026-06-12 |website=Gulf News: Latest UAE news, Dubai news, Business, travel news, Dubai Gold rate, prayer time, cinema |language=en}} In February 2024, the OQ8 Duqm refinery was inaugurated and working at 100% full capacity of 230,000 bpd.{{Cite web |date=2024-05-02 |title=Oman's Duqm refinery units currently working at 100% capacity |url=https://www.hydrocarbonprocessing.com/news/2024/02/omans-duqm-refinery-units-currently-working-at-100-capacity/ |access-date=2026-06-12}} The refinery is a joint venture with Kuwait Petroleum International.{{Cite web |date=2024-02-08 |title=Oman’s Duqm Refinery inaugurated |url=https://theenergyyear.com/news/oman-and-kuwait-inaugurate-the-duqm-refinery/ |access-date=2026-06-12}} The OQ Development Oman]] (POD) for three separate renewable energy projects. In April 2025, all of OQ Chemicals was sold to European-based investment firms Strategic Value Partners (SVP) and Blantyre Capital including all production sites in Germany and the United States.{{Cite web |last= |first= |last2= |first2= |title=Oman's OQ Chem acquired by global investment firms |url=https://www.zawya.com/en/economy/gcc/oman-oq-chem-acquired-by-global-investment-firms-yufccx10 |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=www.zawya.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2025-04-22 |title=Strategic Value Partners and Blantyre Capital acquire OQ Chemicals - European Coatings |url=https://www.european-coatings.com/news/strategic-value-partners-and-blantyre-capital-acquire-oq-chemicals/ |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=www.european-coatings.com |language=en-US}} The lenders' reliability test (LRT) was completed at the OQ8 Duqm refinery in April 2025, providing about $4 billion in shareholder guarantees for the stable transition into commercial operations.{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2025-04-08 |title=OQ8 completes LRT, unlocking $4 billion in shareholder guarantees |url=https://www.omanobserver.om/article/1168757/business/energy/oq8-completes-lrt-unlocking-4-billion-in-shareholder-guarantees |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=Oman Observer |language=en}} The refinery maintained 100% operational rates for all of 2024 and exported more than 4.1 million tonnes of refined products.{{Cite web |last= |first= |last2= |first2= |title=Oman's Duqm Refinery successfully completes Lenders’ Reliability Test |url=https://www.zawya.com/en/economy/gcc/oman-duqm-refinery-successfully-completes-lenders-reliability-test-yravfmiu |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=www.zawya.com |language=en}} ==Operations== The OQ is invested into different main sectors through its network of subsidiaries. These include [[petrochemical]]s, [[refining]] and marketing, [[metal]] and [[mining]] and services. OQ Company runs operations via four main subsidiaries:{{cite web|url=https://www.oman-oil.com/Investment.html|title=Takamul Investment Company SAOC|date=|work=Oman Oil Company|accessdate=January 29, 2019}} * Takamul Investment Company S.A.O.C ** Oman India Fertilizer Co. (OMIFCO) ** [[Oman Refinery Company|Oman Oil Refineries and Petroleum Industries Company]] (ORPIC) ** Salalah Methanol Co. (SMC) ** Minerals Development Oman (MDO) *** Innovation Development Oman Holding (IDO) [Shares transferred to OIA] *** Vale Oman Pelletizing Company (Vale Oman) *** Takatuf Oman *** [[Sohar Aluminium]] Company (SAC) * Oman Oil Company Exploration and Production * Oman Oil Facilities Development Company L.L.C * Oman Oil Duqm Development L.L.C The companies international assets are under direct control of the OOC, which has an international investment unit. These include:{{cite web|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424052970203513604577142112218842228|title=China Gas Flares Up|date=January 5, 2012|work=The Wall Street Journal|accessdate=January 29, 2019}} * [[BlackRock World Mining Trust|Blackrock Metals Company]] – Canada (2.8%) * [[MOL (company)|MOL]] – Hungary (7%) * [[Redes Energéticas Nacionais]] (REN) – Portugal (15%) * Oman Trading International (OTI) – UAE (70%) * Gulf Energy Maritime (GEM) – UAE (30.4%) * Orient Power Company Limited (OPCL) – Pakistan (42.8%) * Planta de Regasification de Sagunto (Saggas) – Spain (7.5%) * Qingdao Lidong Chemical Ltd. – China (30%) * GS Electric Power Solution (GS EPS) – South Korea (30%) * Qingdao Lixing Logistics – China (30%) * Compañia Logística de Hidrocaburos S.A (CLH) – Spain (10%) ==Divisions== ===Feed, food, and agriculture=== Feed, food and agriculture division, covers areas such as [[animal nutrition]], [[crop protection]], [[herbicide]], [[pesticide]] and its handling, and [[human nutrition]].{{Cite web|url=https://oq.com/en/industry-segments/feed-food-and-agriculture|title=Feed, Food & Agriculture | OQ|website=oq.com}} ===Flexible and rigid packaging=== OQ provides flexible packaging for transportation, retail spaces, and for consumers' cupboards.{{Cite web|url=https://oq.com/en/industry-segments/flexible-packaging|title=Flexible Packaging Material Solutions | OQ|website=oq.com}} Some other consumer-facing industry sectors, include cosmetics, electronics, pharmaceuticals, and sporting goods. OQ provides rigid packing products for food, consumer goods, houseware, electronics and industrial packaging.{{Cite web|url=https://oq.com/en/industry-segments/rigid-packaging-and-durables|title=Rigid Packaging & Durables Material Solutions | OQ|website=oq.com}} ===Infrastructure and construction=== OQ is active in [[research and development]] (R&D) of different products.{{Cite web|url=https://oq.com/en/industry-segments/infrastructure-and-construction|title=Infrastructure & Construction | OQ|website=oq.com}} OQ is utilizing its research to develop infrastructure in sectors such as geosynthetics, pipes system, tanks and fittings. ===Lubricants and functional fluids=== OQ provides carboxylic acids, polyols, synthetic polyol ester base oils, and amines.{{Cite web|url=https://oq.com/en/industry-segments/lubricants-and-functional-fluids|title=Lubricants & Functional Fluids | OQ|website=oq.com}} ===Paints and coatings=== OQ's n/iso butyl acetate is used in different applications such as automotive, aerospace, concrete and wood finishes, or as nail polish in cosmetics. Another product, TMP, is used for alkyd and polyester coatings resins and for UV curable alkyd resins, while NPG is used in the production of powder coatings for architectural, automotive, appliances, lawn and garden equipment.{{Cite web|url=https://oq.com/en/industry-segments/paints-and-coatings|title=Paints & Coatings | OQ|website=oq.com}} ===Pharmaceutical and medical care=== OQ produces biocidal alcohols which are used in hand sanitizers and as a specialty amines.{{Cite web|url=https://oq.com/en/industry-segments/pharmaceutical-and-medical-care|title=Pharmaceutical & Medical Care | OQ|website=oq.com}} ==See also== {{Portal|Oman|Energy}} *[[Energy in Oman]] ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== * {{official website|http://www.oq.com}} [[Category:Non-renewable resource companies established in 1982]] [[Category:Oil and gas companies of Oman]] [[Category:National oil and gas companies]] [[Category:Companies based in Muscat, Oman]] [[Category:Companies in the MSM 30]] [[Category:OQ (company)]]
extract:
OQ, formerly known as Oman Oil Company, is an energy investment company headquartered in Muscat, Oman. It is a wholly owned subsidiary of the Government of Oman through the Oman Investment Authority state-owned enterprise.
OQ is involved in sectors such as infrastructure and transportation for energy, oil refining, petrochemical production, oil marketing, and power generating. It operates in 17 countries.
As of June 2023, OQ produces more than  246,000 barrels of oil per day.
